_about: SINGLE-TRANSLATION SHELF: a fourth shelf of one-off English translations of fiction, plays and verse, from the first stretch of the single-translator list: Luise Mühlbach's historical novels by five different translators, Pushkin ×3 (two Captain's Daughters and a Queen of Spades), Dostoevsky's Grand Inquisitor (translated by H. P. Blavatsky), Sienkiewicz's Without Dogma and Sielanka, Hamsun ×2, Ibsen's Early Plays (Orbeck, 1921), Sudermann's Dame Care, Zola ×2, Daudet ×2, Balzac, Anatole France's Queen Pedauque, Coppée ×2, Edmond About, Erckmann-Chatrian, Eugène Sue ×3 (one by Solon De Leon), Jókai ×2, Mikszáth ×2, Kielland ×2, Jonas Lie, Bjørnson (Gosse), Reymont's The Comedienne, Multatuli's Walter Pieterse, Rizal's Friars and Filipinos (Gannett's abridgement), Baroja's Caesar or Nothing, Blasco Ibáñez's Woman Triumphant, Palacio Valdés, Audoux's Marie Claire, Colette's Barks and Purrs, Benoît's Atlantida, Barbusse's The Inferno, Maurois's General Bramble, Jammes, Tieck (Connop Thirlwall), Zschokke, Scheffel's Trumpeter of Säkkingen, Schiller's Turandot, Kotzebue's The Stranger, Iffland's The Lawyers, Corneille's The Cid, Thoma's Moral, Sacher-Masoch's Venus in Furs, Sholem Aleichem, Kompert, Steinberg, Dante's Banquet, Milton's Latin and Italian poems (Cowper), Palamas, the Mârkandeya Purâna, Dandin's Ten Princes, Shinran's Buddhist Psalms, Mathers's Garden of Bright Waters, the Pembroke translations of Mornay and Garnier's Antonius (1592), and anthologies of Malayan, Armenian, Persian, Welsh, Hindustani and Russian verse and tale. Each title gates on its own translator (_surname_by_slug). US public domain. Added 2026-10-10 by lane C (round 48); Adam may veto. No uids minted.
_surname_note: Per title: the translator's name forms.
